motifs.name: bounce
motifs.note: eight notes, entering off the beat and leaning on the threes

motifs.name: bounce_up
motifs.note: the answer, a third higher

motifs.name: patter
motifs.note: fourteen notes, almost all on two pitches: the words do the work

motifs.name: patter_home
motifs.note: thirteen notes through the raised seventh, landing on the stab

motifs.name: tag
motifs.note: verse two's extra two bars: it ends on the leading note, unresolved

motifs.name: step_2
motifs.note: the same shape a step up, bent to stay on the chords

motifs.name: step_3
motifs.note: the same climb, and this time it keeps going -- through the flat sixth of the borrowed minor four -- to the tonic

motifs.name: belt
motifs.note: one note for nine beats over the dominant, a hole, and the two-note pickup that the band is cut for

motifs.name: call
motifs.note: up a fourth to the tonic in two notes, a gap for the words to land in, then it settles

motifs.name: answer
motifs.note: the same rhythm; where the call fell, this one rises

motifs.name: climb
motifs.note: to the top of the tune, held through the half bar the band stops for

motifs.name: climb_ache
motifs.note: the climb over the minor four: one flat on the way up

motifs.name: give
motifs.note: the words go by in one bar so the last one can have the next to itself: a whole bar on the tonic, at the top

motifs.name: sting
motifs.note: the call's rhythm on the dominant of the relative minor: one note from outside the key, resolving up

motifs.name: land
motifs.note: the same trick to end on: six words in a bar, one held for a bar

motifs.name: chant
motifs.note: five notes of the pentatonic scale, for the second voice

motifs.name: slap
motifs.note: the verse bass: root, its octave, root, fifth, with air between. It used to end every bar on a run of sixteenths through the seventh, which driven hard and doubled by the kick was a drum fill in every bar -- the first thing heard, and all that was

motifs.name: disco
motifs.note: the chorus bass: octaves with a hole in them and a run up to the next bar, where it used to be straight eighths

motifs.name: punch
motifs.note: horns: three chord tones up into the next line, in the gap the voice leaves at the end of each one

motifs.name: blip
motifs.note: a chiptune flourish up the chord and back

motifs.name: fanfare
motifs.note: the riff the band opens with and comes back to after each chorus

motifs.name: chime
motifs.note: a music box, before anything else
